importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual variation exists across material types (MS metallic vs FRP fibreglass vs PUF sandwich panel) and size tiers; buyers scan listing tiles to confirm it is a guard cabin and not an office cabin, toilet block, or container before reading any text. Wrong product type = immediate skip.

Size (L×B) and Material are non-interchangeable primary shortlisting criteria — a 4×4 ft MS cabin cannot substitute for a 6×6 ft PUF cabin; listings without these specs cannot be evaluated or priced by buyers.

Price varies 3–5x across the size and material range; Indian B2B buyers compare prices aggressively across sellers once size and material match is confirmed, making price a primary shortlisting lever in this commoditised mid-market category.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with active buyer recall exists in this category; buyers search by size, material, and price rather than manufacturer name, and the market is fragmented across regional fabricators.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional and government buyers evaluate manufacturer status, ISO 9001 certification, and track record of project supply during vendor selection; facility managers and contractors also prefer direct manufacturers over traders for after-sales support.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per sq ft quoting exists for large custom or multi-room orders but is secondary; standard factory-built units are universally quoted per piece and no buyer questions this.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied for a finished factory-built cabin — no buyer would question whether a portable security cabin is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — a 4×4 ft cabin is non-interchangeable with an 8×8 ft cabin and price difference across the size range is 3–5x, making this the primary price-driving configurator.

Defines the product variant within a size tier — MS, FRP, and PUF Panel are non-interchangeable across buyer requirements (corrosion resistance, insulation, durability) with significant price delta between material types.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Standard heights range from 7–8.5 ft and affect site fit, comfort for guard personnel, and compliance with site-specific clearance requirements — sellers need this to confirm the right unit variant.

Relocatability (fixed base vs wheels vs lifting hooks) is a core value proposition of portable cabins and a primary buyer requirement for construction sites where the cabin must be moved as the project progresses.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Material defines the product variant and is non-interchangeable across buyer requirements — sellers need this to confirm they manufacture or stock the requested type and to price it accurately.
Length is the primary dimensional requirement that routes sellers to the correct factory-built size tier and determines the base price of the unit.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers in hot or cold climates specify whether they need an insulated cabin (PUF/rock wool lined) or a non-insulated standard cabin — sellers need this to confirm product fit and price the correct variant, as an MS cabin can be supplied either way.
